disease: Dravet syndrome (SCN1A; NaV1.1 loss-of-function, GABAergic-interneuron haploinsufficiency)

emergence.disease: Dravet syndrome (SCN1A; NaV1.1 loss-of-function, GABAergic-interneuron haploinsufficiency)
emergence.summary: Dravet syndrome (severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy) is a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused in >80% of cases by heterozygous LOSS-of-function (de novo) mutations in SCN1A, which encodes the neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel alpha-subunit NaV1.1 (chr2q24.3). NaV1.1 is expressed predominantly in fast-spiking GABAergic INHIBITORY interneurons (notably parvalbumin-positive interneurons); SCN1A haploinsufficiency lowers NaV1.1, so these interneurons cannot sustain high-frequency firing -> GABAergic inhibition collapses -> cortical networks are DISINHIBITED -> treatment-resistant seizures from the first year of life, with developmental regression, intellectual disability, features of autism and the highest known risk of sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (SUDEP). The kit reads this as the interneuron NaV1.1 sodium-channel current / inhibitory-tone axis driven DOWN (channel LOF -> too few channels, the gate's current is effectively lost -> the interneuron's repetitive-firing current is deficient); the downstream consequence is network excitation UP, but the SWITCH-LEVEL lesion is a loss of inhibitory drive. This is the cystic-fibrosis / K_ATP channel-LOF PATTERN (channel / LOF -> axis DOWN -> restore the channel) carried onto a NEURONAL voltage-gated sodium channel, and it forms a clean MIRROR PAIR with the same release's LQT3 (SCN5A): both are voltage-gated SODIUM channels of the same family, but in OPPOSITE organs (brain interneuron NaV1.1 vs heart NaV1.5), with OPPOSITE mechanisms (LOF vs GOF), OPPOSITE axis (DOWN vs UP) and OPPOSITE levers (restore vs restrain) -- the channelopathy analogue of the Wilson / Menkes copper pair and the SMA / SOD1-ALS motor-neuron pair. IMPORTANT (the honest discipline point): the corrective direction is to RESTORE NaV1.1, but there is NO approved drug that does so -- the switch-level lever is INVESTIGATIONAL. Zorevunersen (STK-001), an antisense oligonucleotide using TANGO (targeted augmentation of nuclear gene output) to suppress a non-productive poison-exon splice event and so UPREGULATE NaV1.1 from the healthy SCN1A allele, is in Phase 3 (EMPEROR); interneuron-targeted dual-AAV split-intein SCN1A gene replacement (e.g. DLX2.0-SCN1A) is preclinical. The APPROVED Dravet drugs -- fenfluramine (Fintepla), cannabidiol (Epidiolex) and stiripentol (Diacomit) -- are recorded as DOWNSTREAM NON-levers on this switch axis: they reduce seizure frequency by serotonergic / endocannabinoid / GABAergic-augmenting and metabolic mechanisms that do NOT restore NaV1.1; treatment remains palliative and there is no cure -- the Rett / trofinetide downstream-agent discipline. So this is the Huntington / XLRP pattern (a resolved, DNA-readable disease whose lead SWITCH-corrective agent is genuinely investigational, direction [F] / adequacy [O]). A timing caveat is honestly noted: NaV1.1 upregulation may be most effective applied early, before chronic circuit rearrangements set in (a magnitude / timing question, [O]). NOTE the sodium-channel-BLOCKER caveat that follows DIRECTLY from the switch read: because the lesion is a LOSS of the inhibitory sodium current, classic sodium-channel BLOCKERS (phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine) tend to WORSEN Dravet seizures -- the engine's axis-DOWN read predicts exactly this contraindication (blocking the already-deficient channel pushes the axis further down), a clean falsifiable consequence. Structural note: SCN1A's promoter gamma 1.2450 (chr2q24.3, AT-rich) is the SECOND-LOWEST gamma in the kit (below only DMD's 1.2388, above F9's 1.2627) -- a shallow-barrier switch. The gamma read is of the SCN1A promoter switch STRUCTURE; the disease lesions are coding / truncating / splice (and ~10% large deletions), outside the promoter firewall. Magnitude [O].
emergence.emergent_axis: GABAergic-interneuron NaV1.1 sodium current / cortical inhibitory tone -- SCN1A haploinsufficiency lowers NaV1.1 in fast-spiking inhibitory interneurons so they cannot fire repetitively, collapsing GABAergic inhibition (axis DOWN) and disinhibiting cortical networks (downstream excitation up). The kit's first NEURONAL ion-channel (epilepsy) axis, the inhibitory-interneuron contrast to LQT3's cardiac NaV1.5 gain

per_gene.note: SCN1A encodes NaV1.1, a neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel alpha-subunit enriched in fast-spiking GABAergic inhibitory interneurons (parvalbumin-positive). Heterozygous LOSS-of-function (truncating / missense / splice; ~10% large deletions; >80% de novo) causes haploinsufficiency -> reduced NaV1.1 -> interneurons cannot sustain high-frequency firing -> loss of inhibition -> the seizures and encephalopathy of Dravet syndrome. chr2q24.3. NCBI official symbol SCN1A. (Milder SCN1A alleles cause GEFS+; certain GAIN-of-function SCN1A alleles cause a distinct familial-hemiplegic-migraine / early epilepsy phenotype -- different (mechanism) reads not conflated here.) Dravet = OMIM 607208. Coding lesions; promoter firewall respected.

levers.push_direction: raise NaV1.1 by upregulating productive SCN1A output from the healthy allele (a TANGO antisense oligonucleotide suppressing a non-productive poison-exon splice) -> restore fast-spiking-interneuron firing -> restore GABAergic inhibition (bring the deficient inhibitory-current axis UP)
levers.mechanism_grade: [O] restored-NaV1.1 / seizure-reduction MAGNITUDE not sequence-derived; the corrective DIRECTION (raise NaV1.1 / inhibitory tone) is forced [F]; efficacy is investigational (Phase 3 EMPEROR ongoing) and may be timing-dependent (most effective applied early, [O])

falsifiers.claim: SCN1A LOF moves the interneuron NaV1.1 / inhibitory-tone axis DOWN (haploinsufficiency reduces fast-spiking-interneuron firing)
falsifiers.falsifier: an SCN1A LOF allele that INCREASED inhibitory-interneuron firing / inhibitory tone, or RAISED NaV1.1 current in interneurons, would refute the channel-off (axis DOWN) read
falsifiers.measurable_by: NaV1.1 current + repetitive firing in Scn1a+/- GABAergic interneurons (patch clamp; parvalbumin-interneuron recordings)

falsifiers.claim: RESTORING NaV1.1 (SCN1A upregulation / gene replacement) is the CORRECTIVE direction -- and BLOCKING the channel WORSENS the disease
falsifiers.falsifier: if RAISING NaV1.1 worsened seizures, or if a sodium-channel BLOCKER reduced seizures in SCN1A-LOF Dravet, the axis-DOWN / restore-direction read is wrong
falsifiers.measurable_by: seizure frequency on SCN1A upregulation vs on a sodium-channel blocker in Scn1a+/- mice / Dravet patients (the phenytoin / carbamazepine worsening is the predicted control)
